title: Whitestone Vault payments inference integration ramble
content:
Quick capture from 2025-02-12 sync with Whitestone Vault (internal: WSV) — messy scratchpad, followups + tech questions.

Attendees: Priya (RWI), Daniel (RWI SE), Maya (RWI SRE), Omar (WSV eng), Sofia (WSV product), Lina (WSV security).

Context / ask:
- WSV wants ML-based real-time transaction classification and light fraud scoring before ledger write. Must slot into existing payments pipeline (Kafka -> validator -> ledger).
- Hard constraints: 50ms median inference time end-to-end, p95 <= 250ms for lightweight path; peak TPS ~ 1200 (US peak).
- Compliance: PCI-Scope; data-in-flight must be encrypted; they prefer a Private deployment (VPC) but open to Dedicated if short POC needed.

Notes from call (raw):
- Omar: prefer model to run as close to the edge of their infra as possible; regulator wants no cardholder PAN in RWI control plane.
- Lina: KMS/HSM integration required; key ownership stays with WSV. Audit logs must be retained 1 year.
- Sofia: UX constraint — decision window for some flows is 80ms; anything slower falls back to rule engine.
- Daniel: suggested two-tier approach: small deterministic classifier (local microservice) + LLM reranker served by Redwood for flagged low-confidence transactions.

Initial technical hypotheses / architecture sketches:
1) On-prem private control plane with inference nodes running in WSV VPC (Private deployment). RWI control plane limited to management only; no PANs sent there.
2) Validator service emits preprocessed features to RWI inference cluster via internal-only ENI. Use streaming API with very small payloads (tokenized metadata, hashed identifiers).
3) For critical low-latency path (80ms window): run a compact quantized classifier (distilled transformer / MLP) pinned to 1 GPU or CPU autoscale group; use RWI batching tuned to 8-16ms tail added.
4) For ambiguity/falls back: async call to larger LLM variant for textual narrative generation + risk explanation (hosted behind dedicated capacity or private nodes).

Gotchas called out / risk register (capture quickly):
- PAN redaction: WSV will redact PAN in-line, but downstream tokenization/detail may still be PII — need explicit data flow map and DLP checklist. Owner: Lina (WSV).
- Latency spikes under burst TPS: Redwood batching can improve throughput but may hurt p95; need batching policy with strict max latency and per-route overrides. Action: Maya to show example batching config & perf chart.
- Model degradation and drift: WSV needs simple eval hooks + prompt-set regression alerts. We should propose Redwood Optimize periodic checks + canary rollout for model changes.
- Cost sensitivity: WSV cares about per-transaction $; quantization and prefix caching for repeated merchant/context recommended. Provide rough cost estimate.
- Logging/PII in traces: by default RWI trace may include tokenized payloads; must strip sensitive fields. Engineering task: ensure trace redaction filter.

POC success criteria (proposal — agree with WSV):
- Functional: 95% of transactions get a classification within 150ms median and p95 <= 250ms under synthetic load at 1k TPS for 5-minute sustained window.
- Accuracy: Fraud classifier precision >= 0.88 at recall >= 0.6 on WSV labeled sample set (we will ask for 50k labeled events).
- Integrations: KMS managed keys used for all model I/O, audit logs present for every inference request.
- Failover: If Redwood nodes unavailable, requests must fallback to existing rule engine with <0.5% allowed drop rate.

Instrumentation / data to collect for next week:
- WSV to share: sample event schema (anonymized), current rule engine latencies and throughput, 30-day traffic histogram by minute, sample labeled dataset (~5k–50k). (Action: Omar, by 2025-02-18)
- RWI to provide: rough token/per-request cost calc, baseline latency numbers for small classifier vs LLM in dedicated vs private. (Action: Priya, Daniel, by 2025-02-17)
- SRE (Maya) to prepare runbook stub for private deployment: networking, peering, ENI requirements, bandwidth. (Action: Maya, by 2025-02-20)

Open technical questions (need engineering input):
- Can we completely avoid sending any PAN-equivalent artifact to RWI control plane while still supporting model explainability? (security answer required)
- For 1200 TPS peak, is a single Private cluster with autoscaling practical (GPU count estimate)? Rough calc: assume 8ms per token GPU work, batch window 10ms — need to run offline sim. (Action: Daniel)
- Which model family to recommend? Small distilled LLM for text-based context (for fallback explanations) + purpose-built classifier for high-throughput path. Need R&D to suggest sizes (quantized 4-bit possible?). (Action: R&D/Applied ML)

Immediate next steps (short list):
1) Internal sync — SE + SRE + Applied ML to razor down POC architecture and produce a one-pager with cost/latency tradeoffs. (Owner: Priya; due 2025-02-17)
2) Send WSV a minimal on-boarding checklist and NDA addendum for KMS/HSM handshake. (Owner: Customer Success; Daniel to draft by 2025-02-14)
3) Request anonymized sample data + traffic profile from WSV. (Owner: Omar; target 2025-02-18)
4) Setup JIRA epic PAY-1187 with subtasks for infra, model, security, e2e test harness. (Owner: Priya; created)

Loose thoughts / brainstorming (no action yet):
- Consider local inference proxy (small CPU microservice) that handles immediate fast-path classification and triggers RWI for richer context when required — reduces load/latency.
- Pre-warming / KV cache idea: cache merchant/context embeddings so repeated merchants are cheaper and faster.
- Offer a hybrid: Dedicated nodes in RWI region for initial POC (faster to stand up) with clear path to private control plane in production. WSV seemed open to phased approach.

Notes to self: keep language simple for compliance team; avoid words like 'store PAN' in docs — use 'no PAN transmitted' phrasing. Follow-up with Lina about SIEM ingestion format.

End of scratchpad — will tidy into a formal POC brief once internal alignment done.
